summary: Scheduled scale-down causes transient 429s after route-weight reshuffle in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:

Customer DataSilo AI reported intermittent 429 responses across several API routes following a scheduled scale-down of their dedicated GPU pool. The pattern started immediately after the autoscaler removed a node while route-weight redistribution (reshuffle) was in progress.

Impact:
- Customer observed ~8-12% of requests returned 429 over a 7-minute window across mixed workloads (embeddings + chat).
- Errors affected production workflows for multiple customers in the same dedicated pool; DataSilo reported failed ingest jobs and degraded user-facing chat latency.
- Business impact: downstream job retries caused backpressure on orchestrators and transient SLA breaches.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-88-west
- Region: us-west-2 (prod-us-west)
- Customer tier: dedicated, reserved capacity 4xA100 nodes (quantized models enabled)
- Traffic mix: 60% chat low-latency, 40% batch embeddings

Steps to reproduce (observed in customer logs / can be simulated):
1. Configure a dedicated pool with route-weighting across 3 routes (chat-high, chat-low, batch-embeds).
2. Schedule policy-driven scale-down (remove 1 node) during light traffic but with ongoing route-weight reshuffle enabled (weight change in Console).
3. Observe: autoscaler drains pod(s), routing layer triggers route-weight rebalance, some in-flight sockets are reassigned.
4. Within 30s of node removal, edge proxies report increased 429 responses for short sessions and for connections which had been reassigned mid-request.

Observed logs / traces (representative):
- gateway: "429 quota_exceeded route=chat-high pool=dp-88-west session_id=..."
- rate-limiter: "token_window_decrement failed: target_node_not_ready during rebalance"
- serving-runtime: "cache-miss + reconnect: kvcache invalidated during host-swap"
- autoscaler: "drain complete node=node-7; trigger route-weight reassign; 3 active sessions migrated"

Initial hypothesis:
- During node removal the route-weight reshuffle briefly double-counts or drop-counts tokens for sessions mid-migration, resulting in transient token-window exhaustion at the logical tenant level.
- Edge proxy connection handoff plus delayed healthcheck reporting caused the token refill scheduler to see an inconsistent view of active connections, producing a local backlog -> 429s.

Mitigation attempted (customer + support):
- Temporarily paused scheduled scale-down to allow gradual manual drain (customer) — mitigated further 429 waves.
- Support toggled route-weight reshuffle to "deferred" in control plane for dp-88-west (temporary) to prevent automatic reassign during active drains.
- Applied short-term smoothing: increased per-route burst window for chat-high by 2x for 15 minutes.

Requested by customer:
- Explanation for root cause and a durable fix to prevent 429s on scheduled maintenance/scale actions.
- Guidance on safe autoscale/drain settings and recommended route-weight change practices for Dedicated pools.
investigation_notes: 03-11 09:14 PDT: Reproduced in staging with same pool config when simulating node removal and simultaneous console route-weight update; observed 5-9% 429s for short-lived sessions.
Token accounting trace showed a ~20s window where route-layer emitted duplicate decrement events for some session ids during reassign handshake.
Healthcheck lag on drained node reported 12-18s before proxy dropped connection from routing tables; this mismatch corresponds to first 429 spike.
KV cache eviction during host swap caused extra upstream retries which incremented token counts on retry paths (possible double-charge).
Related to rate-limiter version deployed on dp-88-west (v1.9.2); staging with patched version (v1.9.4) resolved duplicate decrement in our test runs.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-11: Customer reported first spike at 09:07 PDT. Collected request ids and sample traces; forwarding to infra for deeper trace correlation.

Omar Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: Spun up staging repro with identical route-weight config and simulated drain. Observed duplicate token decrements during session handoff. Building a small patch to guard double-decrement in rate-limiter.
DataSilo (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed that pausing scheduled scale-down eliminated new 429s. Asks for guidance to avoid this in future maintenance windows.
Omar Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Patch applied in canary (rate-limiter v1.9.4). Canary showed no duplicate decrements and 429 rate dropped to <0.1% under same repro load. Preparing rollout plan.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-13: Provided DataSilo a temporary runbook to avoid route-weight changes during node scale events and recommended autoscaler drain_timeout increase from 30s -> 75s.
resolution_notes: Applied hotfix: rate-limiter v1.9.4 prevents duplicate token decrement during session handoff (guard idempotency by session token).
Canary and staged rollout completed across all affected dedicated pools in us-west-2 on 2026-03-13 03:00 UTC (deploy PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4021).
Console: added advisory to disable route-weight reshuffle during automated autoscale operations; change queued for product update (Confluence runbook linked).

Customer guidance sent: avoid simultaneous route-weight edits during scheduled scale events; set drain_timeout >= 60s for heavy session workloads; enable smoothing/burst pool separation for embeddings vs low-latency chat.
Follow-up action: Work with product to add an autoscale-safe flag to Console that prevents reshuffle while drain is in progress (tracked as INT-22021).
follow_up_tasks: INT-22021: Console feature - autoscale-safe mode to suppress route-weight reshuffle during drains
Add monitoring alert: detect duplicate token-decrement events and auto-rollback reshuffle (alert runbook created)
Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-18 with SRE, Product, and Customer Success; include timeline and mitigation effectiveness metrics
